title: Private House Building Permit in Vietnam 2026: Documents and Timeline
desc: Guide to the 2026 private house building permit under the Construction Law 2025 and Decree 217/2026/ND-CP: documents, where to apply and processing time.
summary: Documents, filing venue and processing time for a private house building permit under the Construction Law 2025 and Decree 217/2026/ND-CP.
body: p

From 1 July 2026, building permits are issued under Construction Law No. 135/2025/QH15 and Decree 217/2026/ND-CP. This article summarizes what homeowners need to know when applying for a permit to build a private house, with links to the exact provisions so you can read the original text.
h2
1. Does a private house need a building permit?
p

Under Article 43 of the Construction Law 2025, the investor must hold a building permit before starting construction, except in certain exempt cases. For housing, the most common exemption is a private house of fewer than 7 floors with a total floor area under 500 m² that is not located in areas covered by planning, such as urban development zones, rural residential areas under a general plan, construction areas under a commune general plan, or areas that already have an architectural management regulation.
p
Most houses in wards, townships and planned residential areas still need a permit. For the exempt cases in detail, see Which private houses are exempt from a building permit?
h2
2. Application documents for a private house building permit
p
Under Article 60 of Decree 217/2026/ND-CP, the application of a household or individual consists of:
ol
Application form for a building permit, Form No. 01 in Appendix II of Decree 217/2026/ND-CP.
One of the lawful land documents listed in Article 55 (land use right certificate (sổ đỏ, sổ hồng), or documents qualifying for a certificate, etc.).

The set of design drawings: site plan of the building on the plot with a location diagram; floor plans, elevations and main sections; foundation plan and section with a diagram of water supply, drainage and electricity connections.
A written undertaking to ensure the safety of adjoining buildings.
Fire prevention and fighting procedure results and the design appraisal report (only where required by law).
h2
3. Who may design the house themselves?
p

Under Article 10 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP, the homeowner may organize the design themselves if the house meets all of the following: fewer than 3 floors, no basement, total floor area under 250 m² and height under 12 m. Larger houses must be designed by an organization or individual with the relevant expertise and experience; houses of 7 floors or more, or with 2 or more basements, must also comply with fire prevention and fighting standards.
h2
4. Where to submit the application
p

Under Article 53 of Decree 217/2026/ND-CP, the commune-level People's Committee (commune or ward) where the building is located issues building permits for private houses of households and individuals.
p

Under Article 54, applications are submitted online through the National Public Service Portal; only if an incident makes online submission impossible may they be filed in person at the One-Stop Department or via public postal service.
h2
5. How long does it take to get the permit?
ul
Private houses: 7 working days from receipt of a complete and valid application (new permit, adjustment, repair, renovation, relocation, or fixed-term permit).
Permit extension or reissuance: 5 working days.
If the application is incomplete, the licensing authority notifies the applicant once by email or text message; the homeowner then has 2 working days to supplement it.
h2
6. What happens if you build without a permit or contrary to the permit?
p

From 26 August 2026, violations of construction order are sanctioned under Article 25 of Decree 339/2026/ND-CP. Besides a fine, the building may be ordered to stop construction in order to complete the permit procedure, or the non-compliant part may be ordered to be demolished; it also affects later as-built completion (hoàn công) and registration of the house on the land use right certificate.
note

This article is only a summary for reference and does not replace the legal documents. Some provinces have their own planning and architecture rules; check planning information at the commune or ward People's Committee before designing.
